result.title: Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization: Pre-empting Catastrophic Forgetting via Dynamic Feedback
result.summary: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of LLMs suffers from catastrophic forgetting, and prevailing mitigation strategies struggle to reconcile the plasticity-stability dilemma. To address this, we propose Entropic Control for Homeostatic Optimization (ECHO), a closed-loop control framework. By decomposing the KL divergence, we identify output entropy as a dominant observable component of KL variation. This enables us to leverage entropy as a computationally efficient online proxy to monitor forgetting risks in real-time, bypassing expensive reference-model inference. Consequently, ECHO employs an elastic controller that dynamically modulates the gradient weight of replay data via a proportional control law, using deviations from the pre-trained entropic equilibrium as an error signal. Empirical evaluations across 0.6B to 9B parameter architectures demonstrate that ECHO lies on, and in several comparisons extends, the observed plasticity-stability frontier and maintains high operational robustness against varying data mixing ratios.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ECHO 闭环控制框架，将 KL 散度分解后发现输出熵是其主要可观测成分，于是用相对预训练熵平衡的偏离作为误差信号，经比例控制器动态调节 replay 数据的梯度权重，以缓解 LLM 监督微调的灾难性遗忘。
AI.relevance_reason: 「以输出熵作廉价在线代理、闭环反馈调制训练权重」的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中状态漂移监测与监督配比问题，但原文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
